title: Every start and phase has an exact matching answer

plain_language.question: How long can a prescribed Thue–Morse pattern be followed from any starting point?
plain_language.what_we_learned: There is an exact all-start formula and digit evaluator, plus an attained maximum for every phase and an exact classification of sharp cases.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Compute the actual longest match and distinguish ordinary starts from exceptional long matches without scanning every path.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This is a target-dependent graph result, not every possible pattern search, arithmetic-progression statistic or biological measurement.

exact_statement_and_scope: For digit-parity Thue–Morse t, the graph has edges w−1→w labelled t(w) and w−2→w labelled 1−t(w), for w≥2, and no edge 0→1. A path's kth edge must read t(k). The attained maximum L(v) has a complete closed form for all natural v, with L(0)=1. For v≥1, 3L(v)≤8v−1, with equality exactly at v=3·2^n−1, where L=8·2^n−3. The proved ten-coordinate integer digit recurrence evaluates this maximum. For the own-target graph of s_a(k)=t(k+a), shifting both target and graph, an actual maximum exists at every natural a,v. For v≥1, 3L_a(v)≤8v+5a−1, with equality iff some n≥0 has a≤2^n and v=3·2^n−a−1; then L_a(v)=8·2^n−a−3. Named endpoints are FullHeight.height_isMaximum/height_closed_form, DigitRecurrence.evaluate_isMaximum, PhaseHeight.height_isMaximum and PhaseExtremal.shifted_extremal_iff.
